objective: Implement and test every open issue in refactory-dsh, in ranked order, verified against the circle_packing + annealing_pack running example
rule: Do not stop while any item below is not 'done'. test_work_complete.py fails otherwise, and it requires every item to name its issue, its verification command, and (once done) the evidence observed.
ordered_by: correctness first, then the runtime, then the API, then independent tracks, then the generators, then the future work

items.title: History access, and refuse a proposal that reproduces an existing state (E-duplicate)
items.why: A real bug: duplicates are silently dropped by step(), so batch slots are lost and the run overstates what it tried. Also the prerequisite for the OuterLoop run handle.
items.evidence: 173 passed. tests/test_history.py is new (12 tests): read_run from report.json, the per-candidate fallback for a run with no report, truncation reported, find_runs newest-first and excluding the current run, the context's history/tried/prior_runs, and the prompt carrying both new sections. E-duplicate is refused at the optimizer layer (test_optim.py, 4 new tests) and asserted never to reach step()'s defensive path (attempt == 0), so the slot is refused at the right layer. A real random-optimizer run on circle_packing/adaptive left coded refusals in rejections.jsonl with no lost slot. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_history.py refactory/tests/test_optim.py -q

items.title: str knobs are invisible to the random optimizer and to init's sweep
items.why: Closes the 'declared = optimizable' guarantee, which is the rule the whole seam rests on.
items.evidence: 185 passed. tests/test_str_knobs.py is new (12 tests): an open str knob is sampled by textual mutation and never returns the current value; a str knob with declared values picks one of them; every kind (int, float, bool, str, enum) returns a sample; values validation rejects a non-str kind; the spec round-trips values; the random optimizer proposes string knobs across 40 seeds; the starting sweep includes them; a narrow optimizer is warned about by name at init and reported in knob_coverage; describe() names values and range separately and no longer has an overloaded bounds. A real run on circle_packing/adaptive reports knob_coverage.unreachable == [] and leaves the example test green. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_str_knobs.py refactory/tests/test_example.py -q

items.title: Path-aware evaluation integrity, and the validator's rules stated in the optimizer prompt
items.why: The metric guard is weaker than designed (graph-wide, not path-aware), and every run wastes attempts rediscovering V1-V10.
items.evidence: 218 passed. tests/test_integrity.py is new (12 tests): on_path_nodes excludes a region that cannot reach a terminal; a producer off every path no longer satisfies fact_produced (and V3 does not fire, so it fails on the path); a producer on a path satisfies it; a read satisfied only off-path is refused as V6; the running example's seed still validates. The rules reach the optimizer: a test asserts every code the validator emits appears in RULES and vice versa (AST-parsed, both directions), and that the prompt states V4-V10. summarise_reasons is tested to put the mode-declared rule first and to state the collapsed count. A real autoresearch run used the new prompt: 0 refusals, and its diagnosis cited a previous run's result. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_integrity.py -q

items.title: Mode authoring surface: declared memory with retention, ports, declared surface
items.why: Cross-run priors need somewhere declared to live; the GUI needs to know what a mode publishes.
items.evidence: 218 passed. tests/test_declarations.py is new (17 tests): memory namespace/kind/retention validation, port validation, spec round trips, a run-scoped memory is invisible to another run while a project-scoped one is visible, forget_run_scoped names what it dropped and is quiet the second time, a project memory survives it, kinds cannot be misused, an undeclared namespace is refused, a map keeps keys. V11 refuses a declared port no node on a path writes and accepts one that is written; ports and memory travel in the state and round trip; the report names both and the run records which ports it produced. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_declarations.py -q

items.title: Run durability: artifact schema version, and resume from an append-only log
items.why: A crash loses the run, and unversioned artifacts make an old report read as current.
items.evidence: 213 passed. tests/test_durability.py is new (13 tests): run.json records the layout version; a different version is refused; a run predating versioning is refused rather than guessed; an unreadable sibling is skipped as a prior; the journal records start/candidate/score/epoch_open/epoch_end; resume reproduces an uninterrupted run exactly (best score, evaluations, epochs completed and the whole leaderboard) from three crash points -- before any epoch, between epochs, and from the middle of one; resume does not re-evaluate a scored candidate; a torn final line is ignored; the epoch is not counted twice. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_durability.py -q

items.title: Lower the mode state dict to refactory's IR and run it on DSH
items.why: The stated target: DSH is the runtime, the Python walker is a debug runtime.
items.evidence: 256 passed, 6 skipped. tests/test_lowering.py (16) + tests/test_runner.py (12) + tests/test_equivalence.py (6, marked integration). The equivalence suite passes in full with --run-integration (62s): the spine's own validateGraph accepts the lowered ir; a mode scores the same on DSH as with the walker; the facts match field by field (circles, seed_score, best_score, spent); a node that lies about its facts is refused on the DSH path; and a one-epoch loop with --evaluator dsh reaches the same best score as the walker. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_equivalence.py -q --run-integration
items.verify_note: the equivalence suite is what proves the lowered mode runs on DSH

items.title: Two extension points (Optimizer, OuterLoop) plus all 13 SRF strategies ported
items.why: The search research surface. The abstraction is proven by the ports, not by tests of the abstraction.
items.evidence: 288 passed, 6 skipped. tests/test_outerloop.py (13) covers the seam: a type-1 proposer plugs into the default loop and improves the mode; Run exposes every primitive; evaluating past the budget is refused; attempt spends nothing while evaluate spends one; a strategy can override parent selection, how often it asks, acceptance, archiving and stopping; and a custom control flow cannot get an invalid edit evaluated. tests/test_strategies.py (24) tests each of the 13 ports on its defining behaviour, asserts the port count, and covers registration. A real run of --strategy reflective --optimizer autoresearch logged mutate/mutate/merge and took circle_packing 0.875 -> 1.04. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_outerloop.py refactory/tests/test_strategies.py -q

items.title: Package lifecycle: import, add, remove, enable/disable; workspace root; provenance and trust
items.why: A regression against the deleted glue, and generated packages currently land in the source tree.
items.evidence: 315 passed. tests/test_package_lifecycle.py is new (27 tests): the workspace is not the install tree; a workspace package is discovered, is importable by its normal path, and is reported by the catalogue with where it lives; a name in both roots is refused; add copies, records provenance and trust, refuses a clash, renames with --as, refuses a non-package; import takes a path or refuses a non-path; remove deletes a workspace package, refuses an installed one as read-only, refuses to break a dependent and allows --force; verify reports a missing requirement and a mode whose call does not resolve, and is clean for every installed package; the CLI verbs add, remove, verify, smoke, enable, disable all work and a refusal is a message not a traceback; generated packages are marked. create-mode now writes into the workspace, and annealing_pack declares requires=('circle_packing',). Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_package_lifecycle.py -q

items.title: Generated packages execute as trusted code
items.why: create-mode imports and runs model-written Python with no isolation; the old system sandboxed candidates.
items.evidence: 335 passed. tests/test_sandbox.py is new (20 tests): a well-formed package passes the AST check; it catches a file that does not parse, a missing manifest, a mode with no score(), and a call to eval(); it does not execute anything (a package that raises on import still passes); the environment is an allowlist with secrets dropped and a test asserts the real DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is not visible to a sandboxed run; HOME is redirected; a run past its time limit is killed; a sandboxed run returns its JSON payload; the sandboxed verification reports a broken mode and imports out of process; a sandboxed smoke scores a real mode; promotion is explicit and recorded. create-mode now validates by AST plus a subprocess, never importing what it generated, and its smoke run is sandboxed. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_sandbox.py -q

items.title: Optimizer-facing signals: author priors, refusal findings, block signals, no-op as convergence
items.why: Makes the search better; none of it makes it correct, which is why it follows the correctness work.
items.evidence: 348 passed. tests/test_signals.py is new (13 tests): the mode states guidance and preferred edits and the prompt carries both; a mode with none says so rather than showing nothing; the sampler proposes the preferred operations and still covers the catalogue; an advisory block declares score_effect=none, an unknown tier is refused, and it travels in the state; a dominant refusal is reported as a finding about the catalogue and appears in report.md; a clean run invents no finding; running out of ideas is reported as surface_exhausted with the detail in markdown; a productive run reports no convergence; the report carries attempts per candidate and why that k; and k rises past the configured value on a refusal-heavy batch. A real autoresearch run echoed the guidance in its diagnosis and reached 1.08 with zero refusals. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_signals.py -q

items.title: Run and visualise the outer loop from the GUI, with the loop staying Pythonic
items.why: A user must be able to start a run and read what came out without a terminal.
items.evidence: 29 passed (tests/test_gui_loop.py) + 22 (tests/test_observe.py) + 20 host tool tests + 5 that run the real loop + 20 client card tests. The loop stays a Python process: observe.py writes progress.jsonl (one line per candidate evaluated, not per epoch), diffs a candidate against its parent, and writes manifest.json; console.py is the catalogue + start/watch/stop + artifacts/leaderboard/candidate surface, exported as JSON over a CLI. On the DSH side the `refactory` tool runs that console through the subprocess capability (one action per verb) and projects the payload through output.presentationMeta, and ui-tool registers a tool.call.toolview row under the wire name so the Web view renders the run: state, best score, the progress tail, the leaderboard with each candidate's diff, artifacts. Mounted in the shipped CEO preset. Verified by actually running it: a real headless DSH session with a real model called the tool for `modes`, then started a run, polled status until finished, and read the leaderboard and artifacts (run circle_packing-adaptive-20260913-194618, 6 candidates, best 0.875, 9 artifacts, 18 progress lines on disk). The four presets that drove the deleted refactory_dsh.ops.* modules (create-v2, design-v2, outer-loop, outer-loop-decomposed) were removed; the CEO preset's description no longer names them. REOPENED as deferred: the API surface is done and verified, but the product acceptance is not, and could not be checked here. The three reported defects and their partial diagnosis are in GUI-HANDOFF.md.
items.deferred_reason: Its acceptance is from a browser, and the browser is where it fails: a user reported the hero colliding with its headline, no create/outer-loop entry, and a workspace that cannot be selected. This session's model accepts no image input, so it can see none of that.

items.title: create-mode: survey, strategy, design review, then emit

items.evidence: 362 passed. tests/test_create.py gains 14 tests: the survey names what already exists (both installed modes appear); the strategy prompt carries the survey, the JSON schema and the gate-vs-op distinction; the design prompt carries the chosen approach; a coherent design passes review; review refuses a single-approach choice, a missing chosen/why/score, a closest_existing that is not installed, a design with no knobs, a declared graph that does not hold together (V2), a gate declared with a call instead of an evaluator, and an answer that is not JSON; review accepts 'none'; the gate reloops then fails loudly with its reasons; a bad design is retried with its reasons in the retry prompt. A real create run considered three approaches and named annealing_pack/anneal as closest, passed review, and produced phase_pack/countup smoke-scoring 5.0. items.why: The honest middle path between creating from scratch and hoping a random edit lands.

items.title: Stretch: express the outer loop as a refactory mode
items.why: Future work, but the OuterLoop surface is chosen so this is a lowering rather than a rewrite.
items.evidence: 18 passed. refactory_packages/loop_mode expresses the loop as a graph: init -> forward -> loss -> backward -> optimizer -> step -> scheduler, a gate that loops back to forward or leaves for report. Each node op rehydrates the run from its journal, so a node may run in its own process. The tests assert the graph IS the loop rather than a copy of it: on the same seed and settings it reaches the same best score (0.875) and the same evaluation count as Loop itself, honours both bounds (epochs and max_evaluations), writes the same run directory, and declares ports the run actually writes. score() reads the inner run's best score, so the mode is scorable and an outer loop can search the loop's own knobs (epochs, batch_size, optimizer, elite, attempts, max_evaluations) - the tower closes. Loop gained open_epoch/close_epoch (the nodes that bracket an epoch are not the method that used to), LoopConfig.from_dict, write_pending/read_pending for the propose/install hand-off across processes, and journals `bound` so the report states it durably. Found while building it: `resume=False` on each step deleted the journal between two nodes of the loop's own run.
items.verify_note: the loop-as-mode's end-to-end proof is its DSH run, which is integration-marked

items.title: The GUI can run the loop but cannot author, configure, or manage packages
items.why: create/edit/design, the loop's strategy and settings, and package import/remove/enable/disable are all implemented in Python and reachable from the CLI, but none of them are reachable from the Web view. The capabilities the system exists for are the ones the GUI cannot reach.
items.deferred_reason: Every acceptance criterion is visual: a picker with the right entries, a card that names the strategy, a refusal message on screen. This session's model accepts no image input (read_image refuses it), so it cannot see whether a change worked — the previous hero fix was reasoned from CSS and did not take.
items.deferred_to: https://github.com/akashgit/refactory-dsh/issues/28 — a session running a vision-capable model
items.evidence: Investigated and recorded, not implemented. GUI-HANDOFF.md carries the three rendering/workspace defects found in the same browser session. Verified as already working: all 13 SRF ports plus `default` ship in strategies.py and are selectable through the tool's settings.strategy (confirmed with --strategy reflective); the registry CLI has 9 verbs including add/import/remove/enable/disable. Verified as missing: the `refactory` tool's 8 actions contain no package management, and create/edit/design have no preset and no tool action.

items.title: The SRF strategies record their distinguishing decision instead of applying it
items.why: My `all 13 ported` claim was wrong. `reflective` counts and logs merge-vs-mutate then calls the plain `epoch_step`, so the branch cannot reach the proposal. `reflective_sampler` stores `last_reflection` and never feeds a prompt, while its docstring says the sampling prompt carries prior rejections. `adaptive_meta` logs the meta decision and runs the default step. `research_then_optimize` stores `research_note` and never consumes it — `grep` finds only the two lines that set and log it. 6 of 14 strategies produce byte-identical leaderboards to `default`.
items.evidence: Fixed. Every strategy that only recorded its decision now publishes it through a new `ProposalContext.strategy` channel, and acts on it. `adaptive_meta` widens the batch by 2 on a stall (18 evals vs 16 in the audit rerun, so it now differs from `default` where it did not before). `reflective` builds a real merge — a candidate taking one parent's settings from the other — and falls back to a mutation when the two parents differ structurally rather than in their knobs, because a no-op merge would be refused as E-noop and lose the slot. `reflective_sampler` drops proposals that repeat an edit the run already refused; it reads `self.rejections` for the edits because `Run.rejections()` returns the summarised reasons a prompt wants. `research_then_optimize` and `staged_curriculum` publish their note and stage. Six tests were added that assert the EFFECT rather than the counter, which is exactly what the old tests missed: they asserted `loop.merges >= 1`, so a branch that changed nothing passed. Remaining and honest: with `optimizer=random` the model-facing decisions (research note, curriculum stage) reach a proposer that does not read them, so 4 strategies still produce byte-identical leaderboards on the tiny example — the channel is real and the distinguishing behaviour only shows with a model proposer.

items.title: check_package imports model-written code in the driver process
items.why: Its docstring says `A generated package is never imported here` and the code ends with `load_fresh(name)` -> `importlib.import_module`, then imports every declared ops module and constructs every mode. Only the *structural* check is sandboxed; the semantic half executes untrusted code with full access, which is the whole point of the issue.
items.evidence: Fixed. `check_package` no longer imports the package at all: the whole semantic check — package name, ops modules, every mode's construction, its score, its knobs, every validator rule — moved into `sandbox.verify_sandboxed`'s subprocess. `register` and `smoke` needed the manifest to name what was registered and which mode to run, and were loading the package to get it; both now use the new `sandbox.describe_package`, which reads it out of process. The two orphaned in-process helpers (`load_fresh`, `_check_mode`) are deleted, so there is no longer a function that loads a generated package in the driver. Proven by two new tests in test_create.py that spy on importlib.import_module for the package's module prefix and assert the driver imported nothing while check_package and describe_package ran to a clean result.

items.title: The lowering invents a command string instead of using refactory's callable_name
items.why: The issue says explicitly: do not invent a command string, `FnNode.callable_name` already exists; adopt `AgentNode.post_checks`; adopt Fork/Join. The lowering emits `command: 'python -m refactory_dsh.run <mod>:<fn>'` with `callable_name: None`, and `callable_name`/`post_checks` appear zero times in lowering.py. It runs, but through a convention of our own rather than the seam that was asked for.
items.evidence: Fixed, with a correction to the issue. `callable_name` IS a real `FnNode` field — `factory/workflow/primitives.py:159`, and `factory/workflow/parity.py` round-trips it — so the issue was right that the lowering dropped something. But DSH's spine does not model it: `packages/workflow/workflow-spine/src/types.ts` has `command`, `evaluator_type` and `evaluator_command`, and `callable_name` appears nowhere in the spine's source, which executes the command. So the issue's `do not invent a command string` would have produced a graph whose nodes never run. The lowering now emits **both**: `callable_name` so the IR stays faithful to refactory's language and its tooling can read it, and `command` because that is what the runtime we ship executes. Verified: the lowered graph carries both fields, every declared callable resolves, and the DSH equivalence suite still passes 6. `AgentNode.post_checks` and Fork/Join remain unadopted and are recorded as such rather than silently skipped.

items.title: retention='run' memory is declared but never discarded
items.why: `MemoryStore.forget_run_scoped` exists and is called nowhere. So a run-scoped namespace accumulates exactly like a project one, and the retention policy is a declaration rather than behaviour. The issue's own argument is that run vs project vs global 'is the difference between a memory that dies with the run and one that accumulates'.
items.evidence: Two gaps, both fixed. (1) `MemoryStore.forget_run_scoped` existed with a docstring saying `Called when the run ends` and nothing called it, so a run-scoped namespace accumulated like a project one — and on RESUME a re-evaluated candidate would read its own leftovers, making a resumed run differ from the one it resumed. `Loop._evaluate` now forgets in a `finally`, so a crash or a stop applies the policy too. (2) Found while fixing it: **memory did not cross to DSH at all**. The lowering dropped it and the node runner built its context without a store, so a mode declaring a cross-run prior worked in the walker and silently kept nothing on the runtime that ships — a difference between the runtimes that nothing reported, because the example declares no memory. `write_declarations` now carries the declarations beside the facts, `read_memory_declarations` reads them back, and `run.py` builds the store. Six new tests hold both properties.

items.title: A revision records the mode it came from, not the state it came from
items.why: The issue asks for provenance of `what it was edited from, at which state`. `_revision_source` hands the model the source files, but the output records only `revision_of: <mode id>`. You cannot reproduce or diff a revision against the exact state it was derived from.
items.evidence: Fixed. `_revision_source` handed the model the source *files*, which already worked, but the recorded provenance was `revision_of: <mode id>` alone. A mode is not fixed — the outer loop edits it — so that names a class which may have changed since, and the revision could not be reproduced or diffed against what it actually started from. `edit()` now resolves the source mode once, records its whole `revision_of_state` plus a `revision_of_digest` (the same `candidate_id` the loop uses, so a revision and a candidate that are the same state agree), and returns the digest to the caller. The test asserts the recorded state is a full state dict, that the digest matches the result, and that it identifies the state it was taken from.

items.title: create-v2 and design-v2 as modes in the default package
items.why: The original product had three meta-modes. We have create (a mode), edit (a mode), loop, and design (a mode) — but they are separate entry points, not a package. They belong in one default package, which may need exceptions the mode contract does not otherwise allow.

items.title: A package of modes for frontier mathematics that packs non-Pythonic tools
items.why: Not every tool a mode needs is Python. Lean, mathlib and sympy need installation and a manifest, and the package must be able to declare and provision them. This is the test of whether a package can carry its tools.

items.title: Ship readiness: a person who has never seen this can install, run and extend it
items.why: Everything so far is legible to us. Shipping means a stranger can follow the docs from a clean clone, run the example, create a mode, pack a tool, and know what failed when it does.

verification.method: each item's recorded `verify` command was executed from the repo root
verification.note: two recorded paths were wrong and are corrected here: test_edit.py and test_design.py never existed (edit and design share test_edit_design.py). The loop-as-mode and lowering items now run with --run-integration, because their proof is a real DSH run.

closing_run.model_evidence: The run is model-backed, not a fallback: analysis/generation-0.md holds the proposer's own reasoning, and it cites a prior run's history (/tmp/strat-cli, best 1.04, order=asc) as grounds for the edits it made. That single artifact exercises the history access (#19), the gradient and guidance reaching the prompt (#26), and the reasoning optimizer behind the Optimizer seam (#20).
